doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: School, women pianists and the Chicago style
title: Never giving up music for romance; college and honorary doctorates
summary: She would not abandon music for a man, studied music and sociology at LACC, UCLA and USC, and received two honorary doctorates.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Tell me one more thing. Did you ever think that you would give up your music for romance?
No, I’d have to be hurt. And so I said, “Well, if I give up everything, he’ll just be with another woman. So I’ll just buy a dress and get over him.”
Did you ever think about going to college?
I went to LACC and UCLA, USC.
They think all musicians are stupid. So I said—where’d you go to school? Oh, USC. Where’d you study at…
I like to be a student anyway. And then I got two doctorates.
University of Maryland Eastern Shore and Roosevelt. But I’m always at somebody’s university.
